sights.address: Kuala Lumpur City Centre (KLCC), Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
sights.w: The 452 m twin towers with the double-decker skybridge — KL's defining landmark, once the world's tallest buildings.

sights.address: Gombak, Selangor (Greater Kuala Lumpur), Malaysia
sights.w: A limestone hill of Hindu cave temples reached by 272 rainbow steps under the giant golden Murugan statue; focus of the Thaipusam festival.

sights.address: George Town, Penang, Malaysia
sights.w: The UNESCO-listed old town of clan jetties, shophouses, temples and the famous street-art murals (part of 'Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca').

sights.address: Air Itam, Penang, Malaysia
sights.w: Southeast Asia's largest Chinese Buddhist temple, with the Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas and a 30 m bronze Kuan Yin.

sights.n: Cheong Fatt Tze — The Blue Mansion
sights.address: 14 Leith Street, George Town, Penang, Malaysia
sights.w: The indigo-blue Hakka merchant mansion, a multi-award-winning heritage restoration and film location ('Crazy Rich Asians').

sights.address: Bandar Hilir, Malacca (Melaka), Malaysia
sights.w: The 1511 Portuguese fort gate (Porta de Santiago), the red Dutch Stadthuys/Christ Church and Jonker Street — the heart of UNESCO Malacca.

sights.address: Na Phra Lan Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
sights.w: The 1782 royal palace complex and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha — Thailand's most sacred and most-visited site.

sights.address: 158 Thanon Wang Doem, Bangkok Yai, Bangkok, Thailand
sights.w: The Temple of Dawn, its porcelain-encrusted riverside prang rising over the Chao Phraya.

sights.address: 2 Sanam Chai Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
sights.w: Home of the 46 m gold-leafed Reclining Buddha and the birthplace of traditional Thai massage.

sights.address: 587/10 Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road, Chatuchak, Bangkok, Thailand
sights.w: One of the world's largest weekend markets — 15,000+ stalls of food, crafts, plants and vintage.

sights.address: Doi Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, Thailand
sights.w: The gold-chedi mountain temple above Chiang Mai, reached by a 300-step naga staircase — the city's emblem.

sights.n: Chiang Mai Old City Temples (Wat Chedi Luang & Wat Phra Singh)
sights.address: Old City (within the moat), Chiang Mai, Thailand
sights.w: The walled Old City's Lanna temples — the ruined 14th-century Chedi Luang and the revered Wat Phra Singh.

sights.address: 28 Vo Van Tan Street, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: HCMC's unflinching museum of the Indochina and Vietnam wars — the city's most affecting historical site.

sights.address: Le Loi, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The landmark 1914 central market — street food, textiles and souvenirs in the heart of Saigon.

sights.address: Cu Chi District (Ben Dinh / Ben Duoc), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The vast wartime underground tunnel network northwest of the city — a defining day trip from Saigon.

sights.n: Hoan Kiem Lake, Ngoc Son Temple & the Old Quarter
sights.address: Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
sights.w: Hanoi's civic heart — the legendary lake and its red bridge to Ngoc Son Temple, ringed by the 36-streets Old Quarter.

sights.address: Quang Ninh Province (day trip / cruise from Hanoi), Vietnam
sights.w: The UNESCO seascape of thousands of limestone karst islands — Vietnam's iconic natural wonder.

sights.address: Hoi An, Quang Nam Province, Vietnam
sights.w: The UNESCO-listed trading port of lantern-lit streets, Japanese Covered Bridge and preserved merchant houses.

sights.address: Magelang Regency (near Yogyakarta), Central Java, Indonesia
sights.w: The world's largest Buddhist temple, a 9th-century stupa-mountain of 2,600+ relief panels — UNESCO World Heritage.

sights.address: Sleman (Yogyakarta–Central Java border), Indonesia
sights.w: Indonesia's largest Hindu temple compound, a soaring 9th-century Shiva complex — UNESCO World Heritage.

sights.address: Pecatu, South Kuta, Bali, Indonesia
sights.w: A sea temple perched on a 70 m cliff above the Indian Ocean, famous for sunset and the kecak fire dance.

sights.address: Beraban, Kediri, Tabanan, Bali, Indonesia
sights.w: The much-photographed sea temple on a tidal rock offshore — Bali's classic sunset silhouette.

sights.address: Tegallalang, north of Ubud, Bali, Indonesia
sights.w: The emerald stepped paddies of the subak system — part of Bali's only UNESCO site, the Cultural Landscape of Bali Province.

sights.address: West Jakarta, Jakarta, Indonesia
sights.w: The Dutch-colonial old town around Fatahillah Square, with the Jakarta History Museum and Cafe Batavia.

sights.address: Intramuros, Manila, Philippines
sights.w: The 16th-century Spanish walled city — cobbled streets, bastions and Fort Santiago, the historic core of Manila.

sights.address: General Luna Street, Intramuros, Manila, Philippines
sights.w: The oldest stone church in the Philippines (1607) and a UNESCO 'Baroque Churches of the Philippines' World Heritage site.

sights.address: Ermita, Manila, Philippines
sights.w: The historic seaside park at the site of national hero Jose Rizal's execution, marked by the Rizal Monument.

sights.n: Basilica Minore del Santo Nino & Magellan's Cross
sights.address: Osmena Boulevard / P. Burgos Street, Cebu City, Philippines
sights.w: The country's oldest Catholic relic and church, beside the 1521 cross planted at Magellan's arrival — the cradle of Philippine Christianity.

sights.address: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap, Cambodia
sights.w: The largest religious monument on earth, the 12th-century Khmer temple-city and Cambodia's national symbol — UNESCO World Heritage.

sights.address: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap, Cambodia
sights.w: The walled royal city of Angkor Thom and the Bayon's forest of giant serene stone faces.

sights.address: Sothearos Boulevard, Phnom Penh, Cambodia
sights.w: The Khmer royal palace complex on the riverfront, including the Silver Pagoda with its emerald and gold Buddhas.

sights.n: Luang Prabang Old Town (Wat Xieng Thong)
sights.address: Luang Prabang peninsula, Laos
sights.w: The UNESCO-listed royal town where Lao and French-colonial architecture meet, crowned by the 1560 Wat Xieng Thong and the dawn alms-giving.

sights.address: ~29 km south of Luang Prabang, Laos
sights.w: Turquoise multi-tiered travertine waterfalls in the jungle — Luang Prabang's signature natural excursion.

sights.address: Singuttara Hill, Yangon, Myanmar
sights.w: Myanmar's most sacred Buddhist site — a 112 m gold-plated stupa said to enshrine relics of the Buddha.

sights.address: Bagan, Mandalay Region, Myanmar
sights.w: A plain studded with thousands of 11th–13th-century Buddhist temples and pagodas — UNESCO World Heritage.
